cards.text: It's DONE, friend. Solomon, king of Israel, has finished all the work on the house of the LORD. I can't finish a batch without sneaking three cookies, and this man finished a TEMPLE.

cards.question: Next, Solomon brings in the silver, the gold and all the furnishings his father David had dedicated. Where does he put them?

answers.text: In the treasuries of God's house
In the storerooms of his palace

cards.text: Then Solomon calls in everybody who's anybody. He gathers the elders of Israel in Jerusalem: all the tribal heads and family leaders.

cards.question: Solomon gathers the elders to bring up the ___ of the covenant of the LORD from Zion, the City of David.

cards.text: All the men of Israel come together to the king at the feast in the seventh month. Friend, I've watched four people in a group chat take two WEEKS to pick a day, and Solomon gets a whole nation into one city.

cards.question: When all the elders of Israel have arrived, the Levites take up the ark.
The ark is on the move, but it isn't going up alone. What else do the Levitical priests carry up with it?

answers.text: The Tent of Meeting and its furnishings
The bronze Sea and its twelve oxen
The gold lampstands and the tables

cards.question: Right there before the ark, King Solomon and the whole congregation sacrifice so many sheep and oxen that they could not be ___.

cards.text: So many nobody could count them, and I lose count of chocolate chips at about forty, so I'd have been NO help. Then the priests carry the ark of the covenant of the LORD into the temple, to its place.

cards.question: The priests set the ark of the covenant in its place. Where in the temple is that?

answers.text: The main hall by the lampstands

cards.question: In the Most Holy Place, the ark sits beneath the wings of the cherubim.

cards.text: The cherubim spread their wings over the ark and its poles. The poles are long enough that their ends show from in front of the inner sanctuary but not from outside the Holy Place, and the writer says they're there to this day.

cards.question: Now, the ark of the covenant itself. What's inside it?
The two tablets inside the ark were placed there by ___.

cards.text: Moses put them in at Horeb, where the LORD made a covenant with the Israelites after they came out of Egypt. Those tablets have traveled a LOT farther than I ever did, and the biggest trip of my old life was getting carried across a kitchen to a junk drawer.
Every priest there has consecrated himself, no matter what his division, so NOBODY is sitting this one out. Then the priests come out of the Holy Place.

The Levitical singers take their spot on the east side of the altar: Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun, and their sons and relatives, in fine linen with cymbals, harps and lyres. Friend, the loudest music my old junk drawer ever had was the dead batteries rattling when somebody slammed it shut.

cards.question: Standing with the singers are 120 priests sounding ___.

cards.text: Then the trumpeters and singers join together to praise and thank the LORD with ONE voice. A whole crowd making one sound, and here I am, one stamper who can't hum and stamp at the same time.

cards.question: The trumpeters and singers lift their voices in praise to the LORD. What do they sing about Him?

answers.text: He is good and His loving devotion endures forever
He is mighty and His enemies will scatter forever
He is near and His people will rest in peace now

cards.question: While they praise the LORD, the temple, the house of the LORD, fills with something. What is it?
Because of the cloud, the priests can't stand there to minister.
The priests can't stand there to minister, because the ___ of the LORD filled the house of God.

cards.text: The glory of the LORD fills the house of God, and friend, after all those years I spent waiting for one slice of light in that drawer, I don't even have words. Hold that thought, because this story isn't done.

findings.problem: The joke says the biggest trip of Papa Dorin's old life was being carried across a kitchen to the junk drawer. His backstory says Mother Miller bought him from a closing bakery and took him home, which was a bigger trip. The joke changes his established story instead of only adding a small moment around it.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: Moses first appears in the walkthrough here (and as the answer on card 14), but no card says who he is.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: This is a which-thing question. The wrong answer "Scrolls of David's songs" is made up. It isn't a real detail from somewhere in the Bible.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: The core action in the fact is many voices joining as one. The comparison is one stamper who can't do two things at once (hum and stamp). That is a different action, so the joke doesn't click instantly.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The wrong answers don't match the tone of the right one. "He is near and His people will rest in peace now" sounds padded ("now") and carries a funeral echo ("rest in peace"). The right answer reads as the familiar biblical refrain, so it stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The card opens by retelling what card 8 already covered (the glory of the LORD fills the house of God). It adds no new part of the passage, so it works as a recap. Because the last verse was already asked on a choice card, this card could be only the story-isn't-over line.
